tagline: Italian universal bank with strong capital ratios and diversified financial services
hero_kpi_rationale: The CET1 ratio of 15.17% reflects the strength of Mediobanca's regulatory capital, well above the minimum thresholds set by banking supervisory authorities, demonstrating solid financial resilience against economic shocks and loss absorption capacity.

kpis.name: CET1 Ratio (Tier 1 capital)
kpis.explanation: Tier 1 capital as a percentage of risk-weighted assets taken by the bank.
kpis.description: The CET1 ratio measures capital resistance against risks. A stable level around 15% indicates prudent management.
kpis.signal: Solid financial health, well above the regulatory threshold.

kpis.name: Total Capital Ratio
kpis.explanation: Total capital as a percentage of risks incurred.
kpis.description: This ratio includes all capital layers. Its slight progression shows balance sheet consolidation.
kpis.signal: Capacity to withstand shocks well maintained.

kpis.name: Leverage Ratio
kpis.explanation: Measure of capital relative to total exposure, without risk weighting.
kpis.description: Indicator of gross solvency. The decline reflects exposure growth outpacing capital growth.
kpis.signal: Slight decline, but remains within a prudent range.

kpis.name: Total Risk-Weighted Exposure
kpis.explanation: Total amount of assets weighted by risk.
kpis.description: Steady decline since end of 2023, indicating better risk allocation and prudent portfolio management.
kpis.signal: Continuous reduction in exposure, sign of effective risk management.

kpis.name: CET1 Capital (amount)
kpis.explanation: Amount of the bank's Tier 1 capital in millions of euros.
kpis.description: Capacity to absorb losses. Capital remains elevated despite cyclical pressure on results.
kpis.signal: Slight decline, but high level maintained in absolute terms.

kpis.name: Total Capital (amount)
kpis.explanation: Sum of all regulatory capital layers in millions of euros.
kpis.description: Reflection of balance sheet strength. Slight decline in line with reduction in risk-weighted exposure.

kpis.name: Dividend Per Share
kpis.description: Annual dividend per share, aggregated from yfinance.dividends over the 7 most recent fiscal years declared by the company.
kpis.signal: Dividend per share of 0.63 EUR last year.

kpis.name: Capital Returned (dividends)
kpis.description: Capital returned to shareholders through annual dividends, extracted from yfinance.cashflow over the 4 most recent fiscal years declared.
kpis.signal: Capital returned to shareholders through dividends of 1.153 bn EUR last year.

kpis.name: Payout Ratio
kpis.description: Payout ratio = Dividends paid / Net income, calculated over the 3 most recent fiscal years from yfinance.cashflow and yfinance.income_stmt.
kpis.signal: Portion of net income distributed as dividends: 90.5% last year.

risks.title: Excessive geographic concentration in the Italian market
risks.score_rationale: Standardized tables show that Italy represents the vast majority of consolidated exposures (e.g., ~60% of corporates, ~85% of retail as of 30/06/2024). Dependence on the Italian economic and sovereign cycle is structural and recurrent across all quarters presented.

risks.title: High credit risk on Compass consumer finance portfolio
risks.score_rationale: The retail segment shows RWA at 100% (full weighting) with ~3.5 bn EUR exposure in Italy and significant provisions. Consolidated default exposures remain material (291 m EUR as of 30/06/2024). This risk is recurrent and central to the Compass model.

risks.title: Strategic dependence on Generali stake
risks.score_rationale: Consolidated equity exposures reach ~2.4-2.5 bn EUR with equity RWA of ~7.6-7.9 bn EUR (weighting >300%), reflecting the ~13% stake in Generali. This unique position represents a disproportionate share of regulatory capital and is implicitly mentioned through high-weighted equity items.

risks.title: Competitive pressure on Monaco Wealth Management segment
risks.score_rationale: Monaco exposures (~2.5 bn EUR including 640-654 m EUR secured by mortgages) reflect CMB Monaco (Compagnie Monégasque de Banque) activity. This high-end wealth management segment faces intense international competition from major Swiss and French private banks.

risks.title: Regulatory risk related to evolving CRR/CRD requirements
risks.score_rationale: Tables present compliance with 2024 EBA templates with evolving methodologies (note on general credit adjustments since 2023, exclusion of CIU positions under particular approach). Changes in weighting or methodology directly impact RWA and capital ratios.

risks.title: High-risk corporate exposures in CIB
risks.score_rationale: Consolidated corporate exposures reach ~8.2 bn EUR (exposure value) with ~5.8 bn EUR RWA as of 30/06/2024, implying high average weighting (~70%). Items with particularly high risk (101-142 m EUR) and UK corporate exposures (~1.7 bn EUR) signal concentration in complex deals.

risks.title: Governance and shareholder stability risk
risks.score_rationale: Although not explicitly narrative in this extract, Mediobanca's shareholder structure (Delfin ~19%, Mediolanum, Fininvest) and repeated attempts at strategy influence (MPS bid for Mediobanca in 2025) constitute major governance risk, consistent with the size of equity exposures and model stability.

risks.title: Concentration of interbank exposures and counterparty risk
risks.score_rationale: Exposures to financial institutions are very significant (~6.3 bn EUR consolidated exposure value as of 30/06/2024) with RWA of ~1.75 bn EUR. Strong presence in France (~1.9 bn EUR institutions) and Germany (~1.3 bn EUR) indicates dependence on European interbank markets.

ai_positioning.summary: No mention of artificial intelligence initiatives or strategies in the documents provided.
